items.term: past simple with a finished time: I saw it yesterday
items.gloss: a finished time like yesterday, last year or in 2019 needs the past simple

items.term: present perfect for life experience: Have you ever been to Japan?
items.gloss: experience at some time up to now, with no time given

items.term: When-questions in the past simple: When did you arrive?
items.gloss: when asks about a finished time, so it takes the past simple, not have

items.term: present perfect for unfinished states: I've known her for years
items.gloss: a state that began in the past and continues now: know, live, be

items.term: How long have you …?: How long have you lived here?
items.gloss: asks about duration up to now; not 'How long do you live here?'

items.term: It's been … since: It's been two years since we met
items.gloss: says how much time has passed since an event

items.term: US past simple with just, already and yet: Did you eat yet?
items.gloss: American speech often uses the past simple where British English uses the present perfect

items.term: been vs. gone: She's been to Paris / She's gone to Paris
items.gloss: been = went and came back; gone = went and is still there

items.term: present perfect continuous for duration: I've been waiting for an hour
items.gloss: an activity that started in the past and is still going on

items.term: present perfect continuous for a visible result: Have you been running?
items.gloss: a recent activity explains what we can see or notice now

items.term: present perfect simple vs. continuous: I've written three emails / I've been writing all day
items.gloss: simple for completed amounts; continuous for the activity and how long

items.term: past continuous for an interrupted action: I was cooking when the phone rang
items.gloss: a longer background action interrupted by a short event in the past simple

items.term: was going to for a changed plan: I was going to call you, but …
items.gloss: a past plan or intention that did not happen

items.term: past perfect for the earlier past: When we arrived, the train had left
items.gloss: shows that one past event happened before another past event

items.term: past perfect with by the time: By the time we got there, it had started
items.gloss: the action was already complete at that past moment

items.term: will for instant decisions: I'll get the door
items.gloss: a decision made at the moment of speaking

items.term: will for offers and promises: I'll send it tonight
items.gloss: offers and promises about the future; not present simple 'I send it'

items.term: will for predictions from opinion: I think it'll be fine
items.gloss: a prediction based on belief, often after I think or probably

items.term: going to for plans: I'm going to apply for the job
items.gloss: an intention decided before the moment of speaking

items.term: going to for predictions from evidence: Look at those clouds, it's going to rain
items.gloss: a prediction based on what we can see now

items.term: present continuous for arrangements: I'm meeting Sarah at three
items.gloss: fixed personal plans, usually with a time and other people

items.term: present simple for timetables: The train leaves at 6:15
items.gloss: scheduled events such as transport, classes and programs

items.term: future continuous for an action in progress: This time tomorrow I'll be flying
items.gloss: an action that will be in progress at a certain future time

items.term: future perfect: By Friday, I'll have finished
items.gloss: an action that will be complete before a certain future time

items.term: be about to: The meeting is about to start
items.gloss: something will happen very soon, in the next moments

items.term: stative verbs: I know / I believe, not 'I'm knowing'
items.gloss: verbs of knowing, believing, wanting and owning are not used in continuous forms

items.term: have for possession vs. action: I have a car / I'm having lunch
items.gloss: have = own is stative; have lunch or a meeting can be continuous

items.term: think for opinion vs. process: I think so / I'm thinking about it
items.gloss: think = believe is stative; think = consider can be continuous

items.term: present simple vs. continuous: I work in Zurich / I'm working from home this week
items.gloss: simple for permanent situations; continuous for temporary ones

items.term: gotten as the US past participle: It's gotten worse
items.gloss: American past participle of get for become, receive or obtain

items.term: be being + adjective for temporary behavior: You're being rude
items.gloss: describes how someone is acting now, not a permanent quality

items.term: just for a very recent action: I've just sent it
items.gloss: something happened a moment ago; American English also says 'I just sent it'

items.term: present perfect for news: Scientists have discovered a new species
items.gloss: announces recent news; the details then follow in the past simple

items.term: present perfect with an unfinished period: I've had three coffees today
items.gloss: today, this week and this year are not finished yet

items.term: the first time + present perfect: It's the first time I've tried this
items.gloss: not 'It's the first time I try this'

items.term: present perfect for repeated actions: We've met several times
items.gloss: how many times up to now, with no finished time

items.term: haven't … in + period (US): I haven't seen him in years
items.gloss: American English often uses in instead of for after a negative

items.term: present perfect continuous with lately: I've been feeling tired lately
items.gloss: a recent situation that is still going on; also with recently

items.term: while + past continuous: While I was working, he was sleeping
items.gloss: two longer actions in progress at the same time in the past

items.term: when + past simple vs. past continuous: When he arrived, we ate / were eating
items.gloss: past simple = after he arrived; continuous = already in progress

items.term: past perfect not needed with before / after: After I finished, I left
items.gloss: the time word already shows the order, so the past simple is enough

items.term: when + past simple vs. past perfect: When I arrived, she left / had left
items.gloss: left = after I arrived; had left = before I arrived

items.term: past perfect continuous: I had been waiting for an hour when …
items.gloss: how long an activity went on before a past moment

items.term: future continuous for polite questions: Will you be using the car tonight?
items.gloss: asks about someone's plans without sounding like a request

items.term: hope + present for the future: I hope it goes well
items.gloss: after hope, the present simple often refers to the future

items.term: see in simple vs. continuous: I see / I'm seeing a client tomorrow
items.gloss: I see = I understand; I'm seeing someone = I have a meeting with them

items.term: senses with can: I can hear music, not 'I'm hearing'
items.gloss: hear, see and smell usually take can instead of the continuous

items.term: present continuous for changing situations: Prices are rising
items.gloss: trends and gradual change happening around now

items.term: historical present in stories: So I walk in, and he says …
items.gloss: present tense makes a spoken story or joke more vivid

items.term: have vs. have got in questions: Do you have a minute? (US)
items.gloss: American English prefers do you have; have got is more British

items.term: since vs. for: since Monday / for three days
items.gloss: since + a starting point; for + a length of time

items.term: ago with the past simple: two years ago
items.gloss: ago counts back from now; it comes after the time and takes the past simple

items.term: since + past simple clause: I've known him since we were kids
items.gloss: since + a clause in the past simple marks the starting point

items.term: past perfect with never … before: I had never seen snow before
items.gloss: experience up to a certain point in the past

items.term: future perfect continuous: By June, I'll have been working here for ten years
items.gloss: duration of an activity up to a point in the future

items.term: look and feel in simple or continuous: You look great / You're looking great
items.gloss: with these verbs both forms are correct and mean almost the same

items.term: regular past forms in US English: learned, dreamed, burned
items.gloss: American English prefers -ed; learnt and dreamt sound British

items.term: enjoy / avoid / finish + -ing: I enjoy working here
items.gloss: these verbs take -ing, never to; not 'enjoy to work'

items.term: keep + -ing: He keeps interrupting me
items.gloss: repeat or continue an action, often an annoying one

items.term: spend time + -ing: I spent hours fixing it
items.gloss: not 'spent hours to fix'; also waste time + -ing

items.term: have trouble + -ing: I had trouble finding it
items.gloss: have trouble, difficulty or a hard time + -ing

items.term: be worth + -ing: It's worth trying
items.gloss: the action is useful or will give a good result

items.term: decide / plan / hope + to-infinitive: We decided to wait
items.gloss: these verbs take to + verb, not -ing

items.term: manage to: I finally managed to fix it
items.gloss: succeed in doing something difficult

items.term: tend to: Prices tend to rise in winter
items.gloss: something usually happens or is generally true

items.term: stop + -ing vs. stop + to: I stopped smoking / I stopped to smoke
items.gloss: -ing = quit the activity; to = pause in order to do something

items.term: remember + -ing vs. remember + to: I remember locking it / Remember to lock it
items.gloss: -ing = a memory of the past; to = not forget a task

items.term: forget + to vs. forget + -ing: I forgot to call / I'll never forget meeting her
items.gloss: to = a task not done; -ing = a past experience

items.term: try + -ing vs. try + to: Try restarting it / I tried to open it
items.gloss: -ing = test a method; to = make an effort

items.term: make someone do: She made me laugh
items.gloss: make + object + verb without to; force or cause

items.term: let someone do: Let me know
items.gloss: allow; let + object + verb without to

items.term: get someone to do: I got him to help
items.gloss: persuade someone to do something; get takes to

items.term: suggest + -ing: I suggest leaving early
items.gloss: proposes an action; not 'I suggest to leave'

items.term: suggest + that-clause, not object + to: I suggest you call her
items.gloss: not 'I suggest you to call her'; the same with recommend

items.term: used to + verb: I used to live in Berlin
items.gloss: a past habit or state that is no longer true

items.term: be used to + -ing: I'm used to working late
items.gloss: be familiar with something; to is a preposition here

items.term: get used to + -ing: You'll get used to driving here
items.gloss: become familiar with something new over time

items.term: have something done: I had my hair cut
items.gloss: someone else does a job or service for you

items.term: get something done: We need to get the roof fixed
items.gloss: arrange for a job to be done; also finish a task

items.term: be interested in + -ing: I'm interested in joining
items.gloss: preposition + -ing; not 'I'm interested to join the team'

items.term: think of / about + -ing: I'm thinking of moving
items.gloss: considering a possible plan; not 'thinking to move'

items.term: question word + to-infinitive: I don't know what to do
items.gloss: what, how or where + to + verb for options

items.term: by + -ing for the method: You save money by cooking at home
items.gloss: says how something is done or achieved

items.term: without + -ing: He left without saying goodbye
items.gloss: the action did not happen; not 'without to say'

items.term: instead of + -ing: Instead of complaining, do something
items.gloss: one action replaces another; not 'instead of complain'

items.term: prevent / stop someone from + -ing: The rain stopped us from going
items.gloss: keep someone from doing something

items.term: It's + adjective + to-infinitive: It's hard to say
items.gloss: it stands for the to-clause; a common way to comment

items.term: have someone do (US): I'll have her call you
items.gloss: ask or arrange for someone to do a task; common at work

items.term: it takes + time + to: It took me an hour to get here
items.gloss: says how much time someone needs to do something

items.term: consider + -ing: We're considering moving
items.gloss: think about a possible action; not 'consider to move'

items.term: regret + -ing vs. regret + to: I regret saying that / I regret to say …
items.gloss: -ing = sorry about the past; to = a formal way to give bad news

items.term: go on + -ing vs. go on + to: She went on talking / She went on to become CEO
items.gloss: -ing = continue the same thing; to = do something next

items.term: mean + -ing vs. mean + to: It means waiting / I didn't mean to hurt you
items.gloss: -ing = involve as a result; to = intend

items.term: need + -ing with passive meaning: The car needs washing
items.gloss: same as 'needs to be washed', which Americans usually prefer

items.term: like + to-infinitive or -ing: I like to cook / I like cooking
items.gloss: both are correct; American English often prefers to

items.term: would rather + bare infinitive: I'd rather stay in
items.gloss: prefer to do something; no to after would rather

items.term: help + infinitive with or without to: She helped me move
items.gloss: to is optional; American English usually drops it

items.term: see / hear someone do vs. doing: I saw him leave / leaving
items.gloss: bare verb = the whole action; -ing = part of an action in progress

items.term: didn't use to: I didn't use to like coffee
items.gloss: after did, write use, not used, in negatives and questions

items.term: usually for present habits: I usually walk, not 'I use to walk'
items.gloss: used to is only for the past; present habits take usually

items.term: have something done for bad experiences: I had my phone stolen
items.gloss: something bad happened to you, done by another person

items.term: to as a preposition + -ing: We're committed to improving
items.gloss: after object to or be committed to, -ing follows to

items.term: It's + adjective + for someone + to: It's hard for me to say
items.gloss: for + person names who the comment is about

items.term: find it + adjective + to: I find it hard to focus
items.gloss: it is needed; not 'I find hard to focus'

items.term: adjective + to-infinitive for reactions: I was surprised to hear that
items.gloss: a feeling about an event: happy to help, sorry to hear

items.term: how about / what about + -ing: How about meeting on Friday?
items.gloss: makes a suggestion; -ing or a noun follows about

items.term: good at + -ing: She's good at explaining things
items.gloss: adjective + preposition + -ing; not 'good in explaining'

items.term: would like + to-infinitive: I'd like to ask something
items.gloss: polite want; not 'I'd like asking'

items.term: allow someone to vs. let someone do: They allowed us to leave / let us leave
items.gloss: allow takes to; let takes the verb without to

items.term: prefer + -ing … to + -ing: I prefer walking to driving
items.gloss: prefer one activity over another; to, not than

items.term: be made to in the passive: He was made to wait
items.gloss: make takes to in the passive

items.term: expect someone to: They expect us to finish by Friday
items.gloss: believe or require that someone will do something

items.term: insist on + -ing: She insisted on paying
items.gloss: demand firmly to do something; preposition + -ing

items.term: adjective + active infinitive: The app is easy to use
items.gloss: not 'easy to be used'; the subject is the object of the verb

items.term: give someone something / give it to someone: Give it to me
items.gloss: with a pronoun as the thing, use 'give it to me', not 'give me it'

items.term: afraid of + -ing vs. afraid to: afraid of falling / afraid to ask
items.gloss: of + -ing = fear it may happen; to = too scared to do it

items.term: first conditional: If it rains, we'll stay in
items.gloss: real future possibility; present after if, not 'if it will rain'

items.term: second conditional: If I had more time, I'd travel
items.gloss: unreal present or unlikely future; past after if, would in the result

items.term: past, not would, after if: If I knew, I'd tell you
items.gloss: in unreal conditions use the past after if, not 'if I would know'

items.term: third conditional: If I had known, I would have come
items.gloss: unreal past; avoid 'if I would have known' in writing

items.term: first vs. second conditional: If I get the job / If I got the job
items.gloss: first = realistic; second = unlikely or only imagined

items.term: present simple passive: Coffee is grown in Brazil
items.gloss: facts and processes when the doer is unknown or unimportant

items.term: past simple passive: The bridge was built in 1890
items.gloss: past events where the result matters more than the doer

items.term: present perfect passive: The meeting has been canceled
items.gloss: recent changes or news without naming who did it

items.term: present continuous passive: The room is being cleaned
items.gloss: an action happening to something right now

items.term: future passive: The results will be announced on Monday
items.gloss: future events in official plans and announcements

items.term: passive with modals: It must be done today
items.gloss: modal + be + past participle: can be found, should be checked

items.term: passive with two objects: I was given a laptop
items.gloss: the person usually becomes the subject: I was told, I was offered

items.term: get-passive: He got fired
items.gloss: informal passive for changes, often sudden or bad: got hired, got hurt

items.term: reported statements with backshift: She said she was tired
items.gloss: after a past reporting verb, the tense usually moves back

items.term: will becomes would in reported speech: She said she'd call
items.gloss: a reported promise or prediction uses would

items.term: no backshift for things still true: He said he lives in Boston
items.gloss: keep the present if it is still true now

items.term: reported yes/no questions with if or whether: She asked if I was ready
items.gloss: no do or did, and statement word order

items.term: reported wh-questions: He asked where I lived
items.gloss: statement word order; not 'he asked where did I live'

items.term: reported commands with tell: She told me to wait
items.gloss: tell + person + to-infinitive

items.term: reported negative commands: He told me not to worry
items.gloss: not before to; not 'he told me don't worry'

items.term: reported requests with ask: I asked her to send it
items.gloss: ask + person + to-infinitive for polite requests

items.term: zero conditional: If you heat ice, it melts
items.gloss: general truths and results that always happen; present in both clauses

items.term: first conditional with an imperative: If you see her, tell her
items.gloss: an instruction that depends on a possible situation

items.term: second conditional with could / might: If I had a car, I could drive you
items.gloss: could = would be able to; might = would possibly

items.term: third conditional with could / might: If we'd left earlier, we might have made it
items.gloss: a possible, not certain, different past result

items.term: 'd = had or would: If I'd known, I'd have called
items.gloss: after if, 'd means had; in the result clause it means would

items.term: unless without a second negative: Unless you hurry, you'll miss it
items.gloss: unless already means 'if not'; not 'unless you don't hurry'

items.term: past perfect passive: The files had already been deleted
items.gloss: something done to something before another past event

items.term: modal perfect passive: It should have been done yesterday
items.gloss: criticism or deduction about a past action done to something

items.term: by + agent in the passive: It was written by Toni Morrison
items.gloss: add by only when the doer is important or new information

items.term: passive infinitive: The report needs to be finished
items.gloss: to be + past participle after need, want or have to

items.term: passive -ing form: I hate being interrupted
items.gloss: being + past participle after verbs and prepositions

items.term: be born: I was born in 1990
items.gloss: always past passive for birth; not 'I am born in 1990'

items.term: passive with prepositional verbs: The problem was dealt with
items.gloss: the preposition stays after the verb: was looked after, was paid for

items.term: past events → past perfect in reported speech: He said he had finished
items.gloss: reported earlier events move back to the past perfect

items.term: no backshift after a present reporting verb: She says she's busy
items.gloss: after says or has said, the tense does not change

items.term: modals in reported speech: can → could, must → had to
items.gloss: can, will and must usually move back; could and should stay

items.term: backshift after thought and knew: I thought you were coming
items.gloss: a past thinking verb moves the following clause back

items.term: deny + -ing: He denied taking the money
items.gloss: say that you did not do something

items.term: admit + -ing: She admitted making a mistake
items.gloss: agree that something bad is true, often unwillingly

items.term: refuse to: They refused to pay
items.gloss: say that you will not do something

items.term: promise to: He promised to call back
items.gloss: say that you will certainly do something

items.term: warn someone not to: She warned us not to go
items.gloss: tell someone about a danger so they avoid it

items.term: offer to: She offered to help
items.gloss: the speaker will do it; not 'she offered me to help'

items.term: accuse someone of + -ing: They accused him of lying
items.gloss: say that someone did something wrong

items.term: apologize for + -ing: He apologized for being late
items.gloss: say sorry; for + -ing, not a to-infinitive

items.term: advise someone to: The doctor advised me to rest
items.gloss: recommend an action to someone

items.term: remind someone to: She reminded me to call
items.gloss: help someone remember a task; remind + person + to

items.term: first conditional with a modal: If you finish early, you can go
items.gloss: can, may or should in the result clause instead of will

items.term: passive questions: When was it built?
items.gloss: question word + be + subject + past participle; not 'When it was built?'

items.term: past continuous passive: The car was being repaired
items.gloss: an action in progress at a past moment

items.term: time and place words in reported speech: tomorrow → the next day
items.gloss: here, now and tomorrow change when the time or place changes

items.term: in case of + noun: In case of fire, use the stairs
items.gloss: in notices: if there is; different from in case + clause

items.term: agree to + verb: They agreed to wait
items.gloss: accept to do something; agree with someone = same opinion

items.term: threaten to: He threatened to quit
items.gloss: say that you will do something bad or harmful

items.term: invite someone to: They invited me to speak
items.gloss: ask someone to come or to take part

items.term: blame someone for + -ing: She blamed me for losing it
items.gloss: say that someone is responsible for something bad

items.term: defining relative clause: the woman who called
items.gloss: identifies which person or thing; no commas

items.term: non-defining relative clause: My sister, who lives in Ohio, …
items.gloss: extra information between commas; who or which, never that

items.term: leaving out the object pronoun: the book I read
items.gloss: the object relative pronoun is often dropped, especially in speech

items.term: no extra pronoun in relative clauses: the book that I bought
items.gloss: not 'the book that I bought it'

items.term: where in relative clauses: the city where I grew up
items.gloss: where = in which, after place nouns

items.term: although / even though + clause: Although it was late, we kept going
items.gloss: contrast with a full clause; even though is stronger

items.term: despite / in spite of + noun: Despite the rain, we went
items.gloss: followed by a noun, not a full clause like although

items.term: despite + -ing: Despite feeling sick, she came
items.gloss: the subject of the -ing form is the subject of the main clause

items.term: however as a connector: It's expensive. However, it works.
items.gloss: starts a new sentence with a comma; not used like but

items.term: to-infinitive of purpose: I came to see you
items.gloss: says why; not 'for see' or 'for to see'

items.term: in order to: We cut costs in order to survive
items.gloss: purpose; more formal than to alone

items.term: so that + can / could: I left early so that I could catch the train
items.gloss: purpose, often with a new subject or a modal

items.term: because vs. because of: because it rained / because of the rain
items.gloss: because + clause; because of + noun

items.term: due to + noun: The delay was due to the weather
items.gloss: because of; common in news and official language

items.term: so vs. such: so tired / such a long day
items.gloss: so + adjective; such (a) + adjective + noun

items.term: too vs. not enough: too small / not big enough
items.gloss: too = more than needed; not enough = less than needed

items.term: position of enough: enough time / good enough
items.gloss: enough comes before nouns but after adjectives and adverbs

items.term: either … or: either today or tomorrow
items.gloss: one of two choices

items.term: not only … but also without inversion: She not only wrote it but also directed it
items.gloss: adds a second point with normal word order inside the sentence

items.term: present tense after when / as soon as: I'll call you when I get home
items.gloss: future meaning; not 'when I will get home'

items.term: who for people, which for things: the man who / the box which
items.gloss: not 'the book who'; that is possible for both in defining clauses

items.term: subject relative pronoun cannot be dropped: the man who called me
items.gloss: not 'the man called me' when the pronoun is the subject

items.term: whose as a possessive relative: the colleague whose laptop broke
items.gloss: replaces his, her or their in a relative clause

items.term: where vs. which for places: the town where I live / the town I visited
items.gloss: where replaces in which; a verb with a direct object needs which or that

items.term: when in relative clauses: the day when we met
items.gloss: when = on which, after time nouns; often left out

items.term: what as a relative pronoun: I did what you asked
items.gloss: what = the thing that; not 'that what' or 'which'

items.term: despite the fact that + clause: despite the fact that it rained
items.gloss: despite needs 'the fact that' before a full clause

items.term: however in the middle: The plan, however, failed
items.gloss: however between commas inside the sentence

items.term: nevertheless / nonetheless: The risk is high; nevertheless, we'll try
items.gloss: formal 'but still'; in spite of what was just said

items.term: while meaning although: While I agree, I have some doubts
items.gloss: admits one point before a contrasting point

items.term: yet as a conjunction: simple yet effective
items.gloss: but; adds a surprising contrast, often between adjectives

items.term: so as not to / in order not to: so as not to wake her
items.gloss: negative purpose; more formal than 'to not'

items.term: for + noun for purpose: We went out for dinner
items.gloss: for + noun, not for + verb, to say why

items.term: since / as for reasons: Since you're here, you can help
items.gloss: gives a known reason, usually at the start of the sentence

items.term: so … that / such … that for results: It was so cold that we stayed in
items.gloss: a strong degree and its result

items.term: so much / so many + noun: so many people
items.gloss: not 'such many people'; with nouns use so much or so many

items.term: too … to: too tired to drive
items.gloss: the degree makes the action impossible

items.term: both … and: both fast and cheap
items.gloss: two things are true together

items.term: neither … nor: neither fast nor cheap
items.gloss: not one and not the other; no extra not in the sentence

items.term: as soon as + present perfect: as soon as I've finished
items.gloss: the first action will be complete before the next one

items.term: by the time + present for the future: By the time you arrive, I'll have left
items.gloss: present after by the time; future perfect in the main clause

items.term: once meaning as soon as: Once you've signed, we can start
items.gloss: after something is done or happens

items.term: before / after + -ing: Before leaving, check the lights
items.gloss: -ing after these prepositions when the subject is the same

items.term: apart from: Apart from John, everyone came
items.gloss: except for; also means 'in addition to'

items.term: no but after although: Although it was late, we stayed
items.gloss: not 'Although it was late, but we stayed'

items.term: rather than + verb: Let's walk rather than drive
items.gloss: prefers one action to another

items.term: so that vs. so: I left early so that I could rest / It rained, so we stayed
items.gloss: so that = purpose; so alone = result

items.term: adjective + that-clause: I'm sure it'll work
items.gloss: that is often dropped after sure, glad, afraid and sorry

items.term: after that / afterward: After that, we had dinner
items.gloss: after alone needs a noun or clause; afterward is the American adverb

items.term: everything that, not everything what: Everything she said was true
items.gloss: after everything, all and nothing use that or no pronoun, not what

items.term: instead at the end: Let's walk instead
items.gloss: adverb: in place of the other option just mentioned

items.term: as meaning while: As I was leaving, the phone rang
items.gloss: two things happen at the same time

items.term: therefore in the middle: We therefore conclude that …
items.gloss: formal result connector, often placed after the subject

items.term: until + present for the future: Wait here until I get back
items.gloss: after until, the present simple refers to the future

items.term: not … until for a late time: We didn't start until nine
items.gloss: the action happened only at that later time, not before

items.term: that for people in relative clauses: the guy that I met
items.gloss: that is common for people in speech; who is safer in writing

items.term: a / an for first mention, the for second: I saw a dog. The dog …
items.gloss: new information takes a or an; known information takes the

items.term: a / an with jobs: She's an engineer
items.gloss: not 'She's engineer'; a singular job needs a or an

items.term: how much vs. how many: how much time / how many people
items.gloss: much with uncountable nouns; many with plural nouns

items.term: a lot vs. a lot of: I like it a lot / a lot of people
items.gloss: of only when a noun follows

items.term: some in offers and requests: Would you like some coffee?
items.gloss: some in questions when you expect or want the answer yes

items.term: any in questions and negatives: Do you have any questions?
items.gloss: any in open questions and after not

items.term: no double negative: I didn't see anyone
items.gloss: not 'I didn't see nobody'; use any- after not

items.term: another vs. other vs. the others: another coffee / other people / the others
items.gloss: another + singular; other + plural; the others = the rest

items.term: must vs. have to: I must go / I have to go
items.gloss: must = the speaker's own feeling; have to = a rule; US prefers have to

items.term: don't have to vs. mustn't: You don't have to come / You mustn't tell anyone
items.gloss: not necessary vs. not allowed

items.term: had to for past obligation: I had to work late
items.gloss: must has no past form; use had to

items.term: should for advice: You should see a doctor
items.gloss: advice or a recommendation; ought to is more formal

items.term: must be for present deduction: She must be tired
items.gloss: an almost certain conclusion from evidence

items.term: can't be for present deduction: That can't be right
items.gloss: you are sure something is impossible or not true

items.term: might / may / could be: He might be in a meeting
items.gloss: present possibility: perhaps it is true

items.term: Can I / Could I / May I for permission: Could I borrow your pen?
items.gloss: could is more polite than can; may is formal

items.term: Could you / Would you for requests: Could you send me the file?
items.gloss: polite requests; can you is more informal

items.term: much / far / a lot + comparative: much better, far more expensive
items.gloss: makes a comparison stronger; not 'very better'

items.term: a bit / slightly + comparative: a bit cheaper, slightly higher
items.gloss: shows that the difference is small

items.term: as … as: as fast as / just as good as
items.gloss: equal comparison; as, not than, after the adjective

items.term: not as … as: It's not as hard as I thought
items.gloss: less than; often more natural than 'less … than'

items.term: superlative + ever with present perfect: the best movie I've ever seen
items.gloss: superlative followed by ever, usually with the present perfect

items.term: no double comparative: cheaper, not 'more cheaper'
items.gloss: short adjectives take -er; long ones take more

items.term: one of the + superlative + plural: one of the best restaurants
items.gloss: the noun after one of the is plural

items.term: question tags: It's late, isn't it?
items.gloss: positive statement + negative tag; negative statement + positive tag

items.term: indirect questions: Could you tell me where the station is?
items.gloss: statement word order after a polite opening

items.term: indirect yes/no questions: Do you know if she's here?
items.gloss: if or whether, then statement word order

items.term: subject vs. object questions: Who called you? / Who did you call?
items.gloss: no do when who or what is the subject

items.term: might / may for future possibility: I might come later
items.gloss: perhaps it will happen; might is more common in speech

items.term: the for things both speakers know: Can you close the door?
items.gloss: the when the listener knows which one you mean

items.term: no article with meals, sports and languages: have lunch, play tennis
items.gloss: not 'have the lunch' or 'speak the German'

items.term: a / an for rates and frequency: twice a week, $20 an hour
items.gloss: a or an means per

items.term: no article before next / last + time: next week, last year
items.gloss: next week, last month and this year need no article or preposition

items.term: plenty of: We have plenty of time
items.gloss: more than enough; with plural and uncountable nouns

items.term: no + noun vs. not any: There's no milk / There isn't any milk
items.gloss: the same meaning; no sounds stronger

items.term: each vs. every: each of us / every day
items.gloss: each = one by one, also for two; every = all of three or more

items.term: too much / too many: too much work / too many emails
items.gloss: more than is good; much for uncountable, many for plural

items.term: don't need to for no necessity: You don't need to bring anything
items.gloss: not necessary; American English rarely uses needn't

items.term: be supposed to for rules: You're not supposed to park here
items.gloss: what a rule or other people expect you to do

items.term: can't for rules: You can't park here
items.gloss: not allowed; much more common than mustn't in American English

items.term: be able to in other forms: will be able to, have been able to
items.gloss: can has no future or perfect form, so use be able to

items.term: twice as … as: twice as expensive as
items.gloss: multiples: three times as big as, half as much as

items.term: comparative and comparative: better and better, more and more
items.gloss: shows a change that continues over time

items.term: different from / different than (US): It's different than I expected
items.gloss: different than is normal in American English; from is safe everywhere

items.term: much too + adjective: much too expensive
items.gloss: strengthens too; not 'too much expensive'

items.term: question tag after I'm: I'm late, aren't I?
items.gloss: the tag for I am is aren't I

items.term: answering negative questions: You're not coming? No, I'm not.
items.gloss: yes or no follows the true answer, not the question

items.term: position of all and both: We all agreed / They're both busy
items.gloss: before the main verb, but after be and auxiliaries

items.term: which vs. what in questions: Which one do you want?
items.gloss: which for a limited choice; what for an open choice

items.term: one / ones as a substitute: I'll take the blue one
items.gloss: replaces a countable noun so you do not repeat it

items.term: the for unique things: the sun, the internet, the government
items.gloss: only one exists in our world or situation

items.term: superlative + in / of: the tallest building in the world
items.gloss: in with places and groups; of with periods or numbers

items.term: by far + superlative: by far the best
items.gloss: much better than all the others

items.term: question tags after never / nothing: She never calls, does she?
items.gloss: negative words make the tag positive

items.term: embedded questions after I don't know / I wonder: I don't know what he wants
items.gloss: statement word order; not 'what does he want'

items.term: preposition at the end of questions: Who are you talking to?
items.gloss: in normal speech the preposition goes at the end

items.term: negative questions for surprise: Didn't you get my email?
items.gloss: shows surprise or expects the answer yes

items.term: each other vs. themselves: They help each other
items.gloss: each other = one another; themselves = the same people as the subject
